text:
The Tavrin Valley Agricultural Board declared this season's barley harvest a failure on 14 September, after yields fell 61 percent below the five-year seasonal average.

Roughly 18,400 hectares were affected, according to the Board's "Autumn Harvest Assessment Report No. 7," which was released alongside an emergency session of the Valley Council.

Dr. Ilsa Marenko, Chief Crop Assessor for the Board, said the findings left little room for doubt. "This is not a marginal shortfall. Across the affected hectares, the barley simply did not produce what growers and the valley depend on," she said.

The report sets out the assessment of yields across the valley's barley-growing districts. The Valley Council met in emergency session to consider its findings.

Barley was the crop that failed in the Tavrin Valley this season, the Board confirmed.
